patterns.comment: A body whose %LANGUAGE line states LD or FBD — the ONE place network text is read (the stated language decides how a body is read, never its content). Network text is ST with % lines (volt-cli docs/network-text.html): the ST grammar colours its code, this adds the % lines and the network elements. Ends, by lookahead, at the closing keyword of the unit that owns the body, which the main grammar then colours.
patterns.name: meta.body.network-text

patterns.comment: A % line of a network: %NETWORK "title", %DISABLED, %UNSUPPORTED "shape" #hash — a % first on its line, the key touching it.
patterns.name: meta.line.network-text

patterns.comment: A box is a call, and so is each element of the text: ASSIGN (a coil, a jump, the return), INVERT, RISING and FALLING (a mark on a value), RAIL, BRANCH, BRANCH_SHORTCIRCUIT, OPERAND, COMMENT and the Execute box are the text's own heads, an operator box and MOVE the IDE's; each is coloured where its call opens.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.word.network-text

patterns.comment: A jump and the return are targets of an ASSIGN: => JMP.label, => RETURN.
A mark on a receiver is in its output's name: Q_INVERTED =>, Q_SET =>, Q_RESET =>, q2_SET => on a box's output.
